rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob says he smells Joseph; he describes the olfactory perception as finding because smell is a sense by which something is found.
rows.anchor: لأجد ريح يوسف أشم وعبر عنه بالوجود لأنه وجدان له بحاسة الشم

rows.speaker: أبو بكر ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says afnada can mean grief altered a person's reason, while fannada can mean attributing ignorance to him.
rows.anchor: أفند الرجل إذا حزن وتغير عقله وفند إذا جهل

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asma'i says a man whose speech becomes excessive from senility is called mufannad.
rows.anchor: وعن الأصمعي إذا كثر كلام الرجل من خرف فهو المفند

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf says one says shaykh mufannad but not عجوز مفندة, since she had no sound judgment in youth to lose in old age.
rows.anchor: يقال شيخ مفند ولا يقال عجوز مفندة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob means: if you did not accuse me of senility, when he says he smells Joseph.
rows.anchor: لولا أن تنسبوني إلى الخرف

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil interprets the brothers' charge of old error as worldly misery: Jacob remained in the old misery of grief over Joseph, as in Q 54:24.
rows.anchor: يعني بالضلال ههنا الشقاء / يعني شقاء الدنيا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets old error as Jacob's enduring love for Joseph, which he never forgot, like the brothers' earlier charge in Q 12:8.
rows.anchor: أي لفي حبك القديم لا تنساه ولا تذهل عنه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the brothers spoke harshly and should not have spoken that way to God's prophet.
rows.anchor: قد قالوا كلمة غليظة ولم يكن يجوز أن يقولوها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says they spoke this way because they believed Joseph had died and thought Jacob's fixation had left sound judgment.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن إنما خاطبوه بذلك لاعتقادهم أن يوسف قد مات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle an in فلما أن جاء البشير has no grammatical position; it is sometimes stated and sometimes omitted, as in Q 11:74, with both forms found in Arabic poetry.
rows.anchor: أنه لا موضع لها من الإعراب وقد تذكر تارة كما ههنا

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: The Basrans parse ما أن together as nominative with an implicit verb meaning the herald's arrival appeared.
rows.anchor: هي مع ( ما ) في موضع رفع بالفعل المضمر

rows.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators identify the bearer of good news as Judah, who had carried Joseph's bloodied shirt to Jacob and now brought the shirt to cheer him.
rows.anchor: قال جمهور المفسرين البشير هو يهودا قال أنا ذهبت بالقميص الملطخ بالدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about laying the shirt on his face can mean the herald placed it on Jacob's face or Jacob placed it on his own face.
rows.anchor: طرح البشير القميص على وجه يعقوب أو يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Irtadda means to return to a former state; Jacob regained sight, and the wording attributes the restoration to God as in saying God made a palm tall.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الارتداد انقلاب الشيء إلى حالة قد كان عليها

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say Jacob had become completely blind and God restored his sight at that moment.
rows.anchor: قد عمي بالكلية فالله تعالى جعله بصيرا في هذا الوقت

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others say his sight had weakened from weeping and grief, then strengthened when the shirt and news of Joseph brought joy and relieved his sorrow.
rows.anchor: بل كان قد ضعف بصره من كثرة البكاء وكثرة الأحزان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's knowledge of what others did not know was that Joseph was alive, known to him through the dream; it connects with his earlier statement in Q 12:86.
rows.anchor: علمه بحياة يوسف من جهة الرؤيا

rows.speaker: راوي الخبر
rows.claim: In a report, the herald says Joseph is Egypt's king; Jacob asks about his religion, and on hearing that he remained Muslim says the blessing is now complete.
rows.anchor: هو ملك مصر ، قال : ما أصنع بالملك على أي دين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One report from Ibn Abbas, followed by most commentators, says Jacob delayed asking forgiveness until the predawn hour, thought especially conducive to answered prayer.
rows.anchor: أراد أن يستغفر لهم في وقت السحر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A second report from Ibn Abbas says Jacob delayed until Friday night because it was especially conducive to an answered prayer.
rows.anchor: في رواية أخرى أخر الاستغفار إلى ليلة الجمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that Jacob wanted to learn whether his sons had truly repented with complete sincerity.
rows.anchor: يعرف أنهم هل تابوا في الحقيقة أم لا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A further view says Jacob sought forgiveness immediately, while his promise meant he would continue praying for them; a report says he did so each Friday night for over twenty years.
rows.anchor: أني أداوم على هذا الاستغفار في الزمان المستقبل

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: A report says Jacob prayed for forgiveness for his impatience over Joseph and for his sons' treatment of Joseph, after which God revealed that He had forgiven them all.
rows.anchor: اغفر لي جزعي على يوسف وقلة صبري عليه

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: A report says the sons prayed behind Jacob and Joseph for twenty years; Gabriel then announced that God had answered and established prophetic covenants for them after Jacob, though their prophethood is disputed.
rows.anchor: إن الله تعالى أجاب دعوتك في ولدك وعقد مواثيقهم بعدك على النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the requesters of victory are the messengers, they win and their people lose; if they are the disbelievers, they wrongly think they are right but still fail.
rows.anchor: كان المعنى أن الرسل استفتحوا فنصروا وظفروا بمقصودهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A jabbār is someone arrogant toward obeying and worshipping God; lexicographers list several verbal-noun forms for the word.
rows.anchor: الجبار ههنا المتكبر على طاعة الله وعبادته

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة عن الأحمر
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda, reporting al-Ahmar, gives the forms jabriyya, jabrawa, jabrawut, and jabūra among the word's forms.
rows.anchor: يقال فيه جبرية وجبروة وجبروت وجبورة

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi counts eight verbal-noun forms for jabbār.
rows.anchor: فهي ثمان لغات في مصدر الجبار

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet called a woman who refused his instruction jabbāra, meaning arrogant.
rows.anchor: امرأة حضرت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأمرها أمرا فأبت عليه

rows.speaker: النضر بن شميل
rows.claim: Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl explains ʿanūd as opposition, distancing, or turning away.
rows.anchor: العنود الخلاف والتباعد والترك

rows.speaker: غيره من أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Other linguists derive ʿanīd from ʿand, a side or direction: the person turns aside from the other and keeps away.
rows.anchor: أصله من العند وهو الناحية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jabbār describes an inward trait of arrogance, while ʿanīd describes its outward result: turning away from truth; such a person loses every good and happiness.
rows.anchor: كونه جبارا متكبرا إشارة إلى الخلق النفساني وكونه عنيدا إشارة إلى الأثر الصادر عن ذلك الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warāʾ can name what is hidden from someone, whether in front or behind, as the cited verse and poetry show.
rows.anchor: أن لفظ ( وراء ) اسم لما يوارى عنك

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة وابن السكيت
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda and Ibn al-Sikkit say warāʾ is an antonymic word for both behind and in front; what is behind can turn into what is in front.
rows.anchor: الوراء من الأضداد يقع على الخلف والقدام

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says warāʾ means after, as in the cited line that a person has no destination after God.
rows.anchor: وليس وراء الله للمرء مذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In context, the disbeliever's defeat comes first, and afterward he enters Hell.
rows.anchor: أي ومن بعده الخيبة يدخل جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The drinking clause coordinates with an understood phrase: he is cast into Hell and given pus to drink.
rows.anchor: من ورائه جهنم يلقى فيها ويسقى من ماء صديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This drink is singled out because it seems among the severest forms of punishment, alongside near-death from every side without dying.
rows.anchor: يشبه أن تكون هذه الحالة أشد أنواع العذاب فخصص بالذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣadīd may explain the water as the discharge flowing from the skins of Hell's inhabitants, or as water like pus that God creates in its stench, thickness, and filth.
rows.anchor: الصديد ما يسيل جلود أهل النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that it is actual pus, so repulsive that its foulness prevents the drinker from taking it.
rows.anchor: لأن كراهته تصد عن تناوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image is linked to boiling water that cuts the bowels in Q 47:15 and molten water that scalds faces in Q 18:29.
rows.anchor: وسقوا ماء حميما فقطع أمعاءهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tajarruʿ means taking a drink gulp by gulp continuously; sāgha means to pass down the throat, and asāghahu means to make it go down.
rows.anchor: التجرع تناول المشروب جرعة جرعة على الاستمرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes negating yakādu idiomatically as affirming delayed success: he eventually swallows it after difficulty, like the idiom ما كدت أقوم and Q 2:71.
rows.anchor: أن نفيه إثبات ، وإثباته نفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited melting of stomach contents and skins in Q 22:20 also supports eventual swallowing; repeated sipping in يتجرعه suggests some portion goes down.
rows.anchor: يصهر به ما في بطونهم والجلود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative takes yakādu as near or almost: he does not even come close to swallowing it, as in Q 24:40.
rows.anchor: لم يقرب من رؤيتها فكيف يراها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternatives can be reconciled by saying he does not swallow all of it, or that some reaches his stomach without true swallowing because he takes it unwillingly and cannot tolerate its taste.
rows.anchor: لا يسيغ جميعه كأنه يجرع البعض وما ساغ الجميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Causes of death surround the condemned from every direction, or affect every part of his body, yet he does not die.
rows.anchor: أن موجبات الموت أحاطت به من جميع الجهات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of the next punishment is that it lasts without end.
rows.anchor: أن المراد من العذاب الغليظ كونه دائما غير منقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that each new punishment the condemned faces is more severe than the one before.
rows.anchor: أنه في كل وقت يستقبله يتلقى عذابا أشد مما قبله

rows.speaker: المفضل
rows.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal explains the severe punishment as cutting off breaths and holding them in the bodies.
rows.anchor: هو قطع الأنفاس وحبسها في الأجساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing their punishment, God says all the disbelievers' deeds become void and useless; they will find only punishment and their worldly work will leave no trace, the height of loss.
rows.anchor: أن أعمالهم بأسرها تصير ضائعة باطلة لا ينتفعون بشيء منها

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh supplies an omitted frame for the nominative mathal: their example is in what is recited to you; their deeds as ash then answers a tacit question.
rows.anchor: وفيما يتلى عليكم مثل الذين كفروا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra parses the phrase as the likeness of the deeds of those who disbelieve, with أعمالهم supplying an omitted genitive noun, as in Q 32:7 and Q 39:60.
rows.anchor: التقدير مثل أعمال الذين كفروا بربهم كرماد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other grammatical analyses make the phrase mean the description of the disbelievers is that their deeds are ash, make أعمالهم an appositive to مثل, or treat مثل as an extra particle.
rows.anchor: أن يكون التقدير صفة الذين كفروا أعمالهم كرماد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The simile is that a violent wind scatters ash until it leaves no trace, just as disbelief nullifies deeds completely.
rows.anchor: الريح العاصف تطير الرماد وتفرق أجزاءه بحيث لا يبقى لذلك الرماد أثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view identifies the nullified works as good deeds such as charity, maintaining family ties, honoring parents, and feeding the hungry; disbelief cancels their benefit.
rows.anchor: المراد منها ما عملوه من أعمال البر كالصدقة وصلة الرحم وبر الوالدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view identifies the deeds as idol worship and disbelief that they mistakenly thought was faith and a path to salvation; their labor becomes a burden.
rows.anchor: المراد من تلك الأعمال عبادتهم للأصنام وما تكلفوه من كفرهم الذي ظنوه إيمانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view includes both categories: their real good works and their supposed good works are void, deepening their regret and constituting distant error.
rows.anchor: أن المراد من هذه الأعمال كلا القسمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads الرياح, plural winds; the adjective عاصف grammatically modifies the day for the wind in it, like a rainy day, or means a day of strong winds with الريح omitted; another reading uses genitive.
rows.anchor: قرىء الرياح في يوم عاصف جعل العصف لليوم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra allows interpreting the wording as a day of violent winds or a day whose wind is violent, with wind omitted because it was already mentioned.
rows.anchor: قلت / في يوم ذي عصوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They can draw no useful benefit from what they earned in this world or the next because it has been wholly spoiled.
rows.anchor: أي لا يقدرون مما كسبوا على شيء منتفع به لا في الدنيا ولا في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse supports the view that human beings acquire their actions.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية دالة على كون العبد مكتسبا لأفعاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument moves from ruined deeds to creation: their deeds are annulled because of their disbelief and refusal of servitude, not arbitrarily, since God does not void sincere people's deeds.
rows.anchor: ذلك البطلان والإحباط إنما جاء بسبب صدر منهم وهو كفرهم بالله وإعراضهم عن العبودية

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read خالق as an active participle, predicate of أن, with heavens and earth in a genitive construction, like Q 14:10 and Q 6:95-96.
rows.anchor: على اسم الفاعل على أنه خبر أن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other readers have خلق as a past-tense verb, with heaven and earth as accusative objects.
rows.anchor: والباقون خلق على فعل الماضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recounting the people's grave disbelief and ugly speech, God explains that He delays these disbelievers rather than hastening punishment, showing grace, mercy, and generosity.
rows.anchor: بين أنه يمهل هؤلاء الكفار ولا يعالجهم بالعقوبة

rows.speaker: الطاعنون في عصمة الأنبياء
rows.claim: Critics of prophetic impeccability argue that the verse attributes wrongdoing to all people, and prophets are people, so prophets must sin.
rows.anchor: فأضاف الظلم إلى كل الناس

rows.speaker: الطاعنون في عصمة الأنبياء
rows.claim: They also argue that if prophets were exempt from wrongdoing, destroying every wrongdoer would not entail leaving no creature on earth; the verse therefore makes everyone, including prophets, sinners.
rows.anchor: ما ترك على ظهرها من دابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Q 35:32 divides God's chosen servants into wrongdoers, moderate people, and those foremost in good works; if the latter groups were also wrongdoers, the division would collapse.
rows.anchor: فمنهم ظالم لنفسه ومنهم مقتصد ومنهم سابق بالخيرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Therefore the people in this verse can mean either all sinners deserving punishment or the particular polytheists, including those who attributed daughters to God, so the critics' inference fails.
rows.anchor: إما كل العصاة المستحقين للعقاب أو الذين ذكرهم من المشركين

rows.speaker: بعض الناس
rows.claim: Some use this verse to argue that harm is presumptively forbidden, since permitted harm would have to be either retribution for a prior offense or imposed without such an offense.
rows.anchor: من الناس من احتج بهذه الآية على أن الأصل في المضمار الحرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional is taken to show God did not seize people for their wrongdoing; since many creatures remain, the text is used to reject harm authorized as punishment for earlier crimes.
rows.anchor: وضعت لانتفاء الشيء لانتفاء غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harm imposed without a prior offense is also rejected by consensus, so the verse establishes a general presumption against harms; specific text can make an exception, otherwise harms are forbidden.
rows.anchor: أن يكون مشروعا ابتداء لا على وجه يقع أجزية عن جرم سابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He supports the prohibition with verses against corruption, hardship, and difficulty, plus reports that there is no harming or reciprocal harm and that whoever harms a Muslim is cursed.
rows.anchor: ولا تفسدوا في الأرض بعد إصلاحها

rows.speaker: ومنهم من قال
rows.claim: Some extend the rule to say everything a person wants must be granted and everything disliked must be forbidden because denying or imposing it is harm.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من قال هذه القاعدة تدل على أن كل ما يريده الإنسان وجب أن يكون في حقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that expansive view, analogy is redundant when it agrees with the rule and invalid when it conflicts with the text.
rows.anchor: القياس الذي يتمسك به في إثبات الأحكام

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazilites argue wrongdoing is the people's act, not God's, because the verse assigns it to them; if God created it, punishing them would be injustice by God.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية دالة على أن الظلم والمعاصي ليست فعلا لله تعالى

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They also say the verse's باء marks causation, making human acts effective causes of reward and punishment, as in Q 8:13.
rows.anchor: على أن أعمالهم مؤثرة في وجوب الثواب والعقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent claim that human wrongdoing would destroy every animal raises the problem that animals committed no sin.
rows.anchor: ظاهر الآية يدل على أن إقدام الناس على الظلم يوجب إهلاك جميع الدواب

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i says immediate punishment for disbelief and sin would eliminate human descendants, since every person has an ancestor deserving punishment; animals would disappear too because they serve human interests.
rows.anchor: بما كسبوا من كفر ومعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer says a destruction can punish wrongdoers while testing other people and animals, as occurred in Noah's time.
rows.anchor: أن الهلاك إذا ورد على الظلمة ورد أيضا على سائر الناس والدواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third answer says seizure would stop rainfall and plants, leaving no creature; Abu Hurayra reports a bustard dying in its nest from an oppressor's wrong, and Ibn Mas'ud says a dung beetle nearly perishes in its hole through Adam's children's sin.
rows.anchor: لو آخذهم لا نقطع القطر وفي انقطاعه انقطاع النبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative is that dābbah means a disbeliever rather than every creature, supported by the description of some people as cattle or even further astray in Q 7:179.
rows.anchor: ما ترك على ظهرها من كافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun in عليها refers to earth, though earth was not named; mentioning a creature implies the surface it crawls on, and Arabic often uses this idiom without naming earth.
rows.anchor: عائدة على الأرض ، ولم يسبق لها ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The delay to a specified term allows people to reproduce.
rows.anchor: ولكن يؤخرهم إلى أجل مسمى } ليتوالدوا

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: One interpretation, transmitted by Ata from Ibn Abbas, takes the specified term to be the Day of Resurrection, when most punishment arrives.
rows.anchor: وهو قول عطاء عن ابن عباس أنه يريد أجل القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the term as the end of a lifespan: polytheists receive punishment when their lives end and they leave this world.
rows.anchor: أن المراد منتهى العمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who ascribe to God what they themselves dislike mean that they attribute daughters to Him; jaʿala here means to describe, attribute, or judge, as in the earlier discussion of Q 5:103.
rows.anchor: أي البنات التي يكرهونها لأنفسهم

rows.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Farra and al-Zajjaj parse أن لهم الحسنى as accusative, an apposition to الكذب, yielding the sense that their tongues assert they have good.
rows.anchor: نصب لأن قوله { أن لهم الحسنى } بدل نت الكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claimed good may mean sons for themselves while assigning daughters to God, or their claim to God's approval and the true religion, or their claim to Paradise and reward.
rows.anchor: المراد منه البنون ، يعني أنهم قالوا لله البنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran chiefly establishes four foundations: divinity, prophecy, resurrection, and decree; divinity is primary, so discussion of threats repeatedly returns to it, with proofs ordered from celestial bodies to humans, animals, plants, sea, and earth.
rows.anchor: الإلهيات والنبوات والمعاد ، وإثبات القضاء والقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rain revives earth by producing crops, trees, blossoms, and fruit after barrenness; the proof was discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: خلق السماء على وجه ينزل منه الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call to hear means listening with fairness and reflection; whoever does not listen with the heart is as though deaf.
rows.anchor: سماع إنصاف وتدبر لأن من لم يسمع بقلبه فكأنه أصم لم يسمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse turns from celestial evidence to the wonders of animals; ʿibra was explained earlier as an instructive sign for those with insight in Q 3:13.
rows.anchor: في قوله : { لعبرة لاولي الابصار }

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Hafs from Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i read نسقيكم with a damma on the initial nūn; the remaining readers use a fatha.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ، وأبو عمرو ، وحفص عن عاصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fatha means giving drink, while the damma means furnishing a drink; here the latter suggests abundant, continuing supply, and Abu Ubayd prefers it because drinking is continuous.
rows.anchor: ومن ضم النون فهو من قولك أسقاه إذا جعل له شرابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular masculine pronoun in بطونه can refer to al-anʿām, a collective singular by form but plural feminine by sense, hence the different form in Q 23:21.
rows.anchor: أن لفظ الأنعام مفرد وضع لإفادة جمع

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i parses بطونه as the bellies of what was mentioned; al-Mubarrad says such usage is common in the Quran, as in Q 6:78 and Q 74:54-55.
rows.anchor: قوله : { في بطونه } أي في بطون ما ذكرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This masculine reference works only for grammatically nonreal feminine nouns; it cannot be used for a genuinely female person or maidservant.
rows.anchor: أما الذي يكون تأنيثه حقيقيا ، فلا يجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third grammatical explanation supplies an omitted اللبن: you are given to drink what is in its bellies, namely milk, since not all cattle yield milk.
rows.anchor: والتقدير : نسقيكم مما في بطونه اللبن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Farṯ means the dung or contents of the rumen.
rows.anchor: الفرث : سرجين الكرش . روى الكلبي عن أبي صالح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says fodder settles in the rumen: the lower part becomes dung, the upper blood, and the middle milk; blood enters the veins and milk the udder, while dung remains, so the milk is pure.
rows.anchor: أنه قال : إذا استقر العلف في الكرش صار أسفله فرثا وأعلاه دما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects the claim that blood and milk form in the rumen: repeated slaughter shows neither there, and a process observable in some cases would have been seen.
rows.anchor: فإن هذه الحيوانات تذبح ذبحا متواليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His account is that food is digested first in the stomach or rumen; subtle material is absorbed into the liver and dense residue passes to the intestines.
rows.anchor: فإذا طبخ وحصل الهضم الأول فيه فما كان منه صافيا انجذب إلى الكبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The liver's second digestion turns subtle nourishment into blood and separates bile, black bile, and water; blood then travels through veins and undergoes a third digestion before the udder transforms it into milk.
rows.anchor: ثم ذلك الذي يحصل منه في الكبد ينطبخ فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Males are hot and dry while females are cold and moist; females need added moisture both to form the fetus and to let the body stretch as it grows.
rows.anchor: مزاج الأنثى يجب أن يكون باردا رطبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After birth, moisture that nourished the fetus is redirected to the breast or udder to nourish the infant.
rows.anchor: فعند انفصال الجنين تنصب إلى الثدي والضرع ليصير مادة لغذاء ذلك الطفل الصغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cause that produces milk from blood in females is absent in males, explaining the difference.
rows.anchor: السبب الذي إجله يتولد اللبن من الدم في حق الأنثى غير حاصل في حق الذكر

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators say dung, blood, and milk form in one place: dung at the bottom of the rumen, blood at the top, and milk in the middle.
rows.anchor: المفسرون قالوا : المراد من قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects that account as contrary to observation and experience; if blood formed in the stomach, it would have to be vomited, which is clearly false.
rows.anchor: وقد دللنا على أن هذا القول على خلاف الحس والتجربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains the phrase as a sequence: milk comes from some parts of blood, which comes from subtle parts of the food in the rumen; God filters coarse matter and gives the remainder properties suited to milk and a child's body.
rows.anchor: اللبن إنما يتولد من بعض أجزاء الدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stomach's lower outlet closes while food is needed for digestion and absorption, then opens to release residue; this timed control bespeaks a wise agent.
rows.anchor: فإذا تناول الإنسان غذاء أو شربة رقيقة انطبق ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The liver selectively draws subtle parts while the intestines draw dense residue; reversing those powers would disrupt the body's interests.
rows.anchor: أودع في الكبد قوة تجذب الأجزاء اللطيفة الحاصلة في ذلك المأكول أو المشروب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The liver cooks subtle material into blood, while the gallbladder, spleen, and kidney draw off bile, black bile, and excess water, leaving nourishing blood; this specific allocation requires an all-knowing planner.
rows.anchor: أودع في الكبد قوة هاضمة طابخة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blood nourishes the fetus in the womb, then is redirected to the breast for milk after birth and to the whole body once the child grows; the changing route tracks need and wisdom.
rows.anchor: في الوقت الذي يكون الجنين في رحم الأم ينصب من ذلك الدم نصيب وافر إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tiny nipple pores act as a filter, allowing fine milk through while retaining coarse material, so the milk is pure and suitable for the child.
rows.anchor: أحدث تعالى في حلمة الثدي ثقوبا صغيرة ومسام ضيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inspires the infant to suck, allowing it to benefit from the milk created in the breast.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى ألهم ذلك الصبي إلى المص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Milk contains fat that is hot and moist, water that is cold and moist, and curd that is cold and dry, qualities not present in grass; successive transformations show a wise, merciful creator manages the world for human interests.
rows.anchor: فما فيه من الدهن يكون حارا رطبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sāʾigh means flowing easily and pleasantly through the throat; the wording is linked to Q 14:17.
rows.anchor: جاريا في حلوقهم لذيذا هنيئا

rows.speaker: أهل التحقيق
rows.claim: The creation of milk also demonstrates the possibility of resurrection: water and earth become plants, plants become blood, blood becomes milk, and milk yields fat and cheese, showing God can restore dead bodies to life and reason.
rows.anchor: اعتبار حدوث اللبن كما يدل على وجود الصانع المختار سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After animal benefits, the passage turns to benefits from plants.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر بعض منافع الحيوانات في الآية المتقدمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase from dates and grapes attaches to an omitted نسقيكم, meaning their juice, which is omitted because the preceding verb supplies it; تتخذون منه سكرًا explains the drink.
rows.anchor: ونسقيكم من ثمرات النخيل والأعناب أي من عصيرها

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi says الأعناب coordinates with الثمرات, not النخيل, since grapes themselves are fruit and do not produce another fruit.
rows.anchor: عطف على الثمرات لا على النخيل ، لأنه يصير التقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation takes السكر as wine, a verbal noun of sakira; رزق حسن means other date and grape products such as syrup, vinegar, molasses, dates, and raisins.
rows.anchor: السكر الخمر سميت بالمصدر من سكر سكرا وسكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To explain wine's mention as a blessing, one answer says the sura is Meccan and wine was not forbidden until the Ma'ida revelation.
rows.anchor: تحريم الخمر نزل في سورة المائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer needs no abrogation: wine was useful to the polytheist audience, but separating السكر from good provision signals that it is not good in religious law and is therefore forbidden.
rows.anchor: أنه لا حاجة إلى التزام هذا النسخ

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes sugar as nabīdh: grape, raisin, or date juice boiled until two-thirds evaporates and left to ferment; Abu Hanifa permits it until it intoxicates.
rows.anchor: أن السكر هو النبيذ ، وهو عصير العنب

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: This view argues that the verse presents sugar as a blessing and that the report wine is forbidden in itself means sugar is something other than wine, namely cooked nabīdh.
rows.anchor: ويحتج بأن هذه الآية تدل على أن السكر حلال لأنه تعالى ذكره في معرض الإنعام

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: A third interpretation takes السكر as food; Abu Ubayda supports it with a poetic line where slandering the honorable is made one's food.
rows.anchor: بقول الشاعر : جعلت أعراض الكرام سكرا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the poetic usage better resembles wine: the speaker is metaphorically intoxicated by slandering honorable people.
rows.anchor: هذا بالخمر أشبه منه بالطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The production of these benefits is evidence and blessing; a rational person recognizes that only God can bring about these states and infers a powerful, wise deity.
rows.anchor: علم بالضرورة أن هذه الأحوال لا يقدر عليها إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After signs in animals, God points to human life stages: growth, youthful plateau, slight decline in middle age, and major decline in old age; the transitions show God acts as the mover, not nature.
rows.anchor: في أربع مراتب : أولها : سن النشو والنماء . وثانيهما : سن الوقوف

rows.speaker: الطبائعيون
rows.claim: Naturalist physicians say the body begins from semen and menstrual blood, both hot and moist; heat consumes their moisture and hardens the developing organs and tissues.
rows.anchor: إن بدن الإنسان مخلوق من المني ومن دم الطمث

rows.speaker: الطبائعيون
rows.claim: They say early life has excess moisture that permits growth until about 30 or 35; youth follows when moisture only suffices to preserve innate heat, lasting until about forty.
rows.anchor: الحالة الأولى : أن تكون رطوبة البدن زائدة على حرارته

rows.speaker: الطبائعيون
rows.claim: Naturalists say decline begins when moisture no longer suffices to preserve innate heat: middle age is a subtle decline to sixty, old age an obvious decline to 120.
rows.anchor: أن تقل الرطوبات وتصير بحيث لا تكون وافية بحفظ الحرارة الغريزية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi argues prenatal heat transformed much more moisture into organs than it does after maturity; if heat alone caused development, it should dissipate moisture even faster in the mature body, contrary to observation.
rows.anchor: قبل تولد البدن انتقل جسم المني والدم إلى أن صار عظما وعصبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Innate heat in an adult cannot be merely the small amount present in semen, yet if it grows with the body, strength and health should rise forever; aging therefore is not explained by nature alone.
rows.anchor: الحرارة الغريزية الحاصلة في بدن الإنسان الكامل إما أن تكون هي عين ما كان حاصلا في جوهر النطفة أو صارت أزيد مما كانت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naturalists say heat dries innate moisture, the loss of moisture weakens heat, and the two decline until death; Razi objects that nutrition could replace moisture and that their account circles through mutually dependent causes.
rows.anchor: إن الحرارة الغريزية إذا أثرت في تجفيف الرطوبة الغريزية وقلتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi concludes naturalists' account entails circular reasoning and is false; the stages of aging instead come from the all-powerful, wise, merciful creator, as illustrated by Q 77:20-24.
rows.anchor: فقد صح بالدليل العقلي صدق قوله : { والله خلقكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rational argument confirms that God creates humans, causes death, and causes the shift from youth and health to old age, weakness, and loss of knowledge; these are not effects of nature.
rows.anchor: قد بينا أن السبب الذي ذكروه في صيرورة الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge and power explain these changes: nature cannot distinguish benefit from harm, whereas the world's creator knows benefits and can secure them and avert harms.
rows.anchor: الطبيعة جاهلة لا تميز بين وقت المصلحة ووقت المفسدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arḏal al-ʿumur means the most wretched and weakest stage of life; the wording is linked to Q 26:111.
rows.anchor: رذل الشيء يرذل رذالة وأرذلة غيره

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators say God created people from nothing and takes them at the ends of their appointed lives.
rows.anchor: والله خلقكم ولم تكونوا شيئا ثم يتوفاكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi raises two views on whether the verse's return to the most decrepit age includes Muslims or is restricted to disbelievers, but this excerpt does not give the views.
rows.anchor: هل يتناول المسلم أو هو مختص بالكافر
